text:
cheng: heads up — telemetry shows a sustained spike in svc/foo retries and latency starting ~02:10 UTC. A subset of endpoints (~4/24) are getting 10-20x the normal connections and half of their pods report backlog on GPU queues.
sofia: :thinking: is this the ipvs skew we've seen before or something else?
ben: looks like ipvs stats on the affected nodes show sticky connection funnels. running `ipvsadm -Ln --statistics` shows highly elevated Conns for a few backends.
maya: dropping a quick paste of the ipvs output from node-gpu-12:
```
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InactConn
TCP  10.3.45.10:443 rr
  -> 10.1.12.7:8080             Masq    1      2345       12
  -> 10.1.12.8:8080             Masq    1      23         5
  -> 10.1.12.9:8080             Masq    1      18         3
```
cheng: exact. 10.1.12.7 is a hot potato. conn count on that pod's node is 2.3k while others are ~20. Also saw lots of retransmits reported by `ethtool -S` and kernel dmesg with 'ipvs: can't find' type messages.
raj: I pulled kube-proxy logs on that node — I see repeated `syncService` loops and `failed to apply ipvs dest` warnings after an RTT spike. kube-proxy version is 1.25.6 on the hot nodes, 1.26.3 elsewhere.
sofia: version skew + iptables->ipvs state churn could explain inconsistent hash tables. any MTU mismatches? RDMA enabled on this rack.
ben: yes — node-gpu-12 has MTU 9000, but a recent kernel tweak on the node pool set the host interface to 1500 while the VF is still 9000; kernel reports fragmented RDMA frames occasionally. `ip -d link show` shows mismatched mtu on the bonded interfaces.
maya: that would cause packets to be dropped or retransmitted and could trigger ipvs hash path retries that favor a single endpoint due to timing, right?
cheng: right. we saw east-west latency jump from ~0.6ms to 35-80ms when the hot backend is chosen, likely because packets are being rerouted over slower fallback and causing ipvs to re-evaluate.
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-447, severity=high, services impacted: svc/foo, gpu-pool-a. linked to cluster: us-west-2-prod.
raj: quick mitigation options: 1) cordon the hotspot node, 2) scale more replicas in different AZ and mark preferred endpoints with weights, 3) roll kube-proxy to 1.26.3 across the pool (there's a known ipvs bugfix for dest sync).
sofia: can we avoid pod churn? cordon+drain will disrupt GPU jobs. maybe patch kube-proxy daemonset to increase --ipvs-sync-period and enable --ipvs-atomic to reduce rapid dest churn? also disable RDMA on the affected NICs until we confirm MTU alignment.
ben: I'll run a non-disruptive check: `ipvsadm --set` to rebalance weights for svc/foo on the node and bump weight of healthy endpoints to 5 temporarily. also running `tc -s qdisc show` to verify no queue drops.
maya: logs from the GPU scheduler show retries bubbling up to the scheduler which is re-queueing batches -> cost spike as jobs restart on other nodes. finance flagged a 3x GPU spot usage yesterday. we should include cost playbook in incident notes.
cheng: agreed — immediate plan: (a) annotate node-gpu-12 as `net-investigate` and cordon if packet drops persist, (b) apply a kube-proxy DS patch to set --ipvs-sync-period=15s on canary nodes, (c) set temporary weights via ipvsadm to smooth traffic, (d) schedule full kube-proxy rollout to 1.26.3 after canary verification.
sofia: I'll open a short SR to infra to align MTU across vf/host and disable RDMA on node-gpu-12. ping @maya for GPU workload impact assessment.
maya: noted, will compile job restart list and expected cost delta for 6h window.
deploy-bot: canary patch deployed to kube-proxy daemonset on 3 nodes (node-gpu-10/11/13). monitor for 10m. :rocket:
ben: after 8m the ipvs distribution on canaries looks uniform. conn counts per dest now ~40-60 each instead of funneling.
cheng: keeping this thread up as the single source. if you have packet captures, drop to #eng-infra-pcap with a reference. Will update INC-2026-447 with timeline. :white_check_mark:
